summary: This is a closed GitHub issue (#4046) in the pypa/setuptools repository reporting that the setuptools 68.2.0 change "Record normalized requirements in dist.metadata object" breaks building ROS2 Python packages with colcon, because colcon feeds setup.py output into a compiler and the new repr-style output causes a SyntaxError. Reporter owend says reverting is the easiest fix; maintainer abravalheri asks whether 68.2.1 was tried, asasine confirms 68.2.1 mitigates the issue, and owend closes it as fixed with 68.2.1 on Sep 12, 2023.
one_line: GitHub issue reporting that setuptools 68.2.0 broke colcon builds of ROS2 Python packages, fixed in 68.2.1.
key_facts: GitHub issue #4046 in the pypa/setuptools repository was titled "[BUG] Internal 68.2.0 change breaks all ROS2 python packages".
The issue was opened by user owend on Sep 12, 2023.
The reported problem was caused by the setuptools 68.2.0 change described as "Record normalized requirements in dist.metadata object", commit a641c78.
The reporter stated the change probably breaks all downstream Python packages built for ROS2 using colcon.
The reported error output was a SyntaxError: invalid syntax caused by '_normalized_install_requires': {'setuptools': <Requirement('setuptools')>}.
The reporter said the root cause is that colcon feeds output from setup.py into a compiler and now receives a non-compilable string representation with extra <> characters.
The reporter noted that the colcon design flaw had been "known" since 2021, referencing colcon/colcon-core#454.
Builds using setuptools 68.1 worked, and the reporter suggested reverting the change as the easiest fix.
Maintainer abravalheri asked whether the reporter had tried setuptools 68.2.1.
User asasine confirmed that 68.2.1 mitigates the issue.
abravalheri argued that serialising arbitrary objects with repr and expecting them to parse as Python would be a very bold decision.
owend closed the issue as fixed with 68.2.1, and abravalheri closed it as completed on Sep 12, 2023.
The issue was labeled bug and Needs Triage, later also Waiting User Feedback.
The issue thread lists 3 participants: owend, abravalheri, and asasine.
